articles.title: Bevacizumab in patients with hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia and severe hepatic vascular malformations and high cardiac output.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: The only treatment available to restore normal cardiac output in patients with hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (HHT) and cardiac failure is liver transplant. Anti-vascular endothelial growth factor treatments such as bevacizumab may be an effective treatment.
OBJECTIVES: To test the efficacy of bevacizumab in reducing high cardiac output in severe hepatic forms of HHT and to assess improvement in epistaxis duration and quality of life.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PATIENTS: Single-center, phase 2 trial with national recruitment from the French HHT Network. Patients were 18 to 70 years old and had confirmed HHT, severe liver involvement, and a high cardiac index related to HHT.
INTERVENTION: Bevacizumab, 5 mg per kg, every 14 days for a total of 6 injections. The total duration of the treatment was 2.5 months; patients were followed up for 6 months after the beginning of the treatment.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURE: Decrease in cardiac output at 3 months after the first injection, evaluated by echocardiography.
RESULTS: A total of 25 patients were included between March 2009 and November 2010. Of the 24 patients who had echocardiograms available for reread, there was a response in 20 of 24 patients with normalization of cardiac index (complete response [CR]) in 3 of 24, partial response (PR) in 17 of 24, and no response in 4 cases. Median cardiac index at beginning of the treatment was 5.05 L/min/m(2) (range, 4.1-6.2) and significantly decreased at 3 months after the beginning of the treatment with a median cardiac index of 4.2 L/min/m(2) (range, 2.9-5.2; P < .001). Median cardiac index at 6 months was significantly lower than before treatment (4.1 L/min/m(2); range, 3.0-5.1). Among 23 patients with available data at 6 months, we observed CR in 5 cases, PR in 15 cases, and no response in 3 cases. Mean duration of epistaxis, which was 221 minutes per month (range, 0-947) at inclusion, had significantly decreased at 3 months (134 minutes; range, 0-656) and 6 months (43 minutes; range, 0-310) (P = .008). Quality of life had significantly improved. The most severe adverse events were 2 cases of grade 3 systemic hypertension, which were successfully treated.
CONCLUSION: In this preliminary study of patients with HHT associated with severe hepatic vascular malformations and high cardiac output, administration of bevacizumab was associated with a decrease in cardiac output and reduced duration and number of episodes of epistaxis.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: clinicaltrials.gov Identifier: NCT00843440.

articles.title: [Vascular ultrasonography].
articles.abstract: Vascular ultrasound plays an important role in the visual depiction of arteries, veins, and changes of tissue in lymphatic diseases. In the case of arteries, this ranges from endothelial dysfunction over measuring the increase of intima media thickness to the detection of stenoses, occlusion, or aneurysm. Ultrasound helps to differentiate in functional arterial diseases such as primary and secondary Raynaud's syndrome as well as arterial compression syndromes like entrapment syndrome of different arterial regions or the chronic exceptional compartment syndrome of the lower leg. Ultrasound plays a central role in the diagnosis of rare arterial diseases like large vessel vasculitis, arterial dissection, cystic adventitial degeneration, and the differentiation of vascular malformation especially in children, thus, permitting ultrasound-guided intervention and follow-up controls. In venous thrombosis, sonography is the primary imaging method, while follow-up controls help in the prediction of recurrent venous thrombosis. Ultrasound is a tool to determine the cause and severity of chronic venous insufficiency and allows different therapeutic procedures for the treatment of varicose veins to be visually monitored.

articles.title: Endovascular treatment of cervical giant perimedullary arteriovenous fistulas.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Giant perimedullary arteriovenous fistulas (GPMAVFs) located in the cervical region are a rare pathology with distinctive characteristics.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate clinical presentation and different endovascular treatment options of cervical GPMAVFs and review previously published data in the literature regarding cervical GPMAVFs.
METHODS: Six patients with cervical GPMAVFs were found in the spinal vascular malformations database of our group collected between 1990 and 2009. Endovascular techniques and treatment outcomes were evaluated and compared with other published series.
RESULTS: Clinical presentations were progressive motor deficit (5 patients), hematomyelia (1 patient), meningeal syndrome (1 patient), and respiratory arrest and gait apraxia (1 patient). Three patients were treated by the transarterial approach. One patient was treated by the transvenous approach due to previous embolizations resulting in a proximal occlusion and preventing a safe transarterial approach. A transvenous approach was used in another patient due to complex arterial anatomy. In 1 patient, direct percutaneous puncture of the venous pouch was necessary because of previous proximal occlusion of the arteries. All embolizations resulted in complete occlusions with clinical improvement, and there was no recanalization during a mean follow-up of 21 months.
CONCLUSION: Transarterial embolization of cervical GPMAVFs is safe and effective when it is done in highly experienced centers. Cervical GPMAVFs that cannot be accessed by the transarterial technique due to their complex angioarchitecture can be treated by transvenous embolization or direct puncture of the venous pouch.

articles.title: Case report: gastrointestinal hemorrhage caused by a pancreas transplant arteriovenous fistula with large psuedoanuerysm 9 years after transplantation.
articles.abstract: Reported cases of arteriovenous fistulae in transplant recipients are uncommon. We present a case of an arteriovenous fistula associated with a large pseudoaneurysm in the root of the small bowel mesentery of a pancreas transplant. Uniquely, in our case, the arteriovenous fistula presented with an episode of gastrointestinal (GI) hemorrhage 9 years postoperatively. Radiographic imaging including coronal computed tomography angiogram and conventional angiogram demonstrated an arteriovenous fistula in the patient's pancreas transplant between the distal superior mesenteric artery (SMA) and superior mesenteric vein (SMV) with 6 cm aneurysmal dilatation. The tremendous flow in the fistula in the root of the graft small intestine mesentery led to graft duodenal mucosal congestion and lower GI hemorrhage. After successful embolization of the SMA-SMV fistula and pseudoaneurysm using interventional radiographic techniques, the arteriovenous fistula remained thrombosed. The patient had no further episodes of GI bleeding and her endoscopic evaluation was otherwise negative. The presence of arteriovenous fistulae and pseudoaneurysms in pancreas transplant recipients is uncommon, but has been previously documented. This case is further distinguished from previous reports by the notable 9-year interval between transplantation and the onset of hemorrhage. Historically, symptomatic vascular malformations have been associated with significant patient morbidity and mortality. Successful patient management involves timely and accurate diagnosis and intervention.

articles.title: Microcatheter navigation using a large compliant balloon placed in a cortical vein during transvenous access.
articles.abstract: Transvenous embolization (TVE) has emerged as the new approach for the curative treatment of brain arteriovenous malformations (bAVMs), though challenges persist in navigating microcatheters through dural venous sinuses. This video article demonstrates a novel balloon-assisted technique to facilitate microcatheter navigation in a complex case of bAVM. A large compliant Copernic RC balloon was temporarily placed in a cortical vein, serving as a buttress to guide the microcatheter into the draining vein. This method enabled the successful cannulation and advancement of a microcatheter in a draining cortical vein using a large compliant balloon without complications. The case highlights the technical feasibility and safety of this approach in TVE for challenging bAVM cases. neurintsurg;18/12/2323/V1F1V1Video 1 Microcatheter navigation using a large compliant balloon placed in a cortical vein during a transvenous access.

articles.title: [Microsurgical treatment of non-bleeding cerebral arteriovenous malformations].
articles.abstract: Treatment of non-bleeding cerebral arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) causes a lot of controversy among neurosurgeons around the world. The most discussed issue is choosing the method and indications for a certain treatment option. Despite the accumulated data, including the results of randomized studies, there is no consensus on this issue among experts. The purpose of this review is to analyze current concepts of the management and reasonability of microsurgical treatment of non-bleeding cerebral AVMs based on the latest published studies.

articles.title: Volume-staged versus dose-staged stereotactic radiosurgery outcomes for large brain arteriovenous malformations: a systematic review.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE Several recent studies have improved our understanding of the outcomes of volume-staged (VS) and dose-staged (DS) stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) for the treatment of large (volume > 10 cm3) brain arteriovenous malformations (AVMs). In light of these recent additions to the literature, the aim of this systematic review is to provide an updated comparison of VS-SRS and DS-SRS for large AVMs. METHODS A systematic review of the literature was performed using PubMed to identify cohorts of 5 or more patients with large AVMs who had been treated with VS-SRS or DS-SRS. Baseline data and post-SRS outcomes were extracted for analysis. RESULTS A total of 11 VS-SRS and 10 DS-SRS studies comprising 299 and 219 eligible patients, respectively, were included for analysis. The mean obliteration rates for VS-SRS and DS-SRS were 41.2% (95% CI 31.4%-50.9%) and 32.3% (95% CI 15.9%-48.8%), respectively. Based on pooled individual patient data, the outcomes for patients treated with VS-SRS were obliteration in 40.3% (110/273), symptomatic radiation-induced changes (RICs) in 13.7% (44/322), post-SRS hemorrhage in 19.5% (50/256), and death in 7.4% (24/323); whereas the outcomes for patients treated with DS-SRS were obliteration in 32.7% (72/220), symptomatic RICs in 12.2% (31/254), post-SRS hemorrhage in 10.6% (30/282), and death in 4.6% (13/281). CONCLUSIONS Volume-staged SRS appears to afford higher obliteration rates than those achieved with DS-SRS, although with a less favorable complication profile. Therefore, VS-SRS or DS-SRS may be a reasonable treatment approach for large AVMs, either as stand-alone therapy or as a component of a multimodality management strategy.

articles.title: Unruptured Brain Arteriovenous Malformations: Primary ONYX Embolization in ARUBA (A Randomized Trial of Unruptured Brain Arteriovenous Malformations)-Eligible Patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: In light of evidence from ARUBA (A Randomized Trial of Unruptured Brain Arteriovenous Malformations), neurovascular specialists had to reconsider deliberate treatment of unruptured brain arteriovenous malformations (uBAVMs). Our objective was to determine the outcomes of uBAVM treated with primary embolization using ethylene vinyl alcohol (ONYX).
METHODS: Patients with uBAVM who met the inclusion criteria of ARUBA and were treated with primary Onyx embolization were assigned to this retrospective study. The primary outcome was the modified Rankin Scale score. Secondary outcomes were stroke or death because of uBAVM or intervention and uBAVM obliteration.
RESULTS: Sixty-one patients (mean age, 38 years) were included. The median observation period was 60 months. Patients were treated by embolization alone (41.0%), embolization and radiosurgery (57.4%), or embolization and excision (1.6%). Occlusion was achieved in 44 of 57 patients with completed treatment (77.2%). Forty-seven patients (77.1%) had no clinical impairment at the end of observation (modified Rankin Scale score of <2). Twelve patients (19.7%) reached the outcome of stroke or death because of uBAVM or intervention. Treatment-related mortality was 6.6% (4 patients).
CONCLUSIONS: In uBAVM, Onyx embolization alone or combined with stereotactic radiosurgery achieves a high occlusion rate. Morbidity remains a challenge, even if it seems lower than in the ARUBA trial.

articles.title: Therapeutic plasma exchange and continuous renal replacement therapy for severe dengue with multiorgan failure: a case report and focused review.
articles.abstract: Severe dengue can progress to acute liver failure, haemolysis, encephalopathy, shock, and multiorgan dysfunction, but the role of therapeutic plasma exchange in treatment remains uncertain. We report a 17-year-old adolescent with NS1-positive dengue managed with continuous renal replacement therapy, therapeutic plasma exchange, and comprehensive intensive care, and provide a focused narrative review of therapeutic plasma exchange in severe dengue. The patient developed abrupt massive intravascular haemolysis, profound anaemia, thrombocytopenia, coagulopathy, encephalopathy requiring invasive mechanical ventilation, oliguric acute kidney injury, shock, and acute liver failure. She also met five of eight HLH-2004 criteria for secondary haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis. Continuous renal replacement therapy was initiated before three therapeutic plasma exchange sessions, beginning with an exchange of 1·5 estimated plasma volumes using fresh frozen plasma. Haemodynamic, hepatic, renal, and coagulation parameters subsequently improved. Secondary infection and haemothorax requiring video-assisted thoracoscopic drainage complicated recovery; she was discharged 38 days after admission. Published evidence on the use of therapeutic plasma exchange in severe dengue consists mainly of case reports, small series, and observational cohorts. Therapeutic plasma exchange can be considered an adjunctive rescue therapy in selected refractory cases, particularly acute liver failure or thrombotic microangiopathy phenotypes, but its independent benefit, optimal timing, prescription, and target population remain undefined.

articles.title: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis complicated by anti-GBM nephritis: a clinicopathological case of PR3-ANCA-positive double-positive disease.
articles.abstract: Anti-glomerular basement membrane (anti-GBM) nephritis is an autoimmune disease characterized by rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis, which is histologically defined by crescentic glomerulonephritis and linear immunoglobulin G (IgG) deposition. Granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA) is an anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitis characterized by necrotizing granulomatous inflammation and is strongly associated with proteinase 3 (PR3)-ANCA. The coexistence of anti-GBM nephritis and ANCA-associated vasculitis, termed "double-positive" disease, is increasingly recognized, although most cases are associated with myeloperoxidase-ANCA. A 77-year-old woman presented with fever, hearing loss, and renal dysfunction. Renal biopsy revealed crescentic glomerulonephritis with linear IgG deposition, and serum anti-GBM antibodies were positive, consistent with anti-GBM nephritis. She was diagnosed with GPA based on refractory otitis media, PR3-ANCA positivity, and granulomatous inflammation with multinucleated giant cells on renal biopsy. The patient was treated with glucocorticoids, intravenous cyclophosphamide, and plasma exchange (14 sessions), followed by avacopan. Renal function was preserved, and no progression to end-stage renal disease was observed at 10 months. We report a rare clinicopathological case of PR3-ANCA-positive double-positive disease with coexisting GPA and anti-GBM nephritis. This case highlights the characteristic clinicopathological features supporting the coexistence of these two diseases. The possible relationship between GPA and anti-GBM disease remains hypothetical and requires further investigation.

articles.title: Therapeutic plasma exchange improves short-term survival in patients with acute-on-chronic liver failure: A randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: This randomized controlled trial (RCT) evaluated the efficacy and safety of therapeutic plasma exchange (TPE) versus standard medical therapy (SMT) in acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF).
APPROACH AND RESULTS: In this single-center, open-label RCT (February 2022-March 2025), we randomly (1:1) assigned 194 adult patients (aged 18-60 y) with ACLF [European Association for the Study of the Liver-Chronic Liver Failure Consortium (EASL CLIF-C) grades 1-3b] to receive SMT plus 5 sessions of TPE (n=97) or SMT alone (n=97). The primary outcome was all-cause mortality at 28 days. Secondary outcomes included 90-day mortality, changes in prognostic scores, resolution of organ failures, infections, and adverse events. Baseline characteristics were comparable between groups. Seventy-two (74.2%) patients completed 3 sessions of TPE, while 56 (57.7%) received all 5 sessions. Hemodynamic instability was the leading cause for discontinuation of TPE (18/41 patients, 43.9%). The 28-day mortality was significantly lower with TPE (43 patients, 44.3%; 95% CI: 34.2%-54.8%) than SMT (62 patients, 63.9%; 95% CI: 53.5%-73.4%), p =0.006; absolute risk reduction: 19.6% (95% CI: 5.8%-33.3%). Ninety-day mortality was similar between groups. TPE resulted in greater reductions in ammonia and higher rates of resolution of hepatic and coagulation failure by day 7 as compared with SMT. Subgroup analysis did not reveal significant heterogeneity across ACLF grade or etiology. Dyselectrolytemia and shivering were the most common complications after TPE.
CONCLUSION: TPE significantly improves 28-day survival and organ failure resolution in patients with ACLF, but does not reduce 90-day mortality [CTRI/2022/01/039094].

articles.title: Intranasal delivery of a ROS-activatable myeloperoxidase inhibitor alleviates Alzheimer's-like symptoms and pathology.
articles.abstract: Chronic neuroinflammation and oxidative stress are important contributors to Alzheimer's disease (AD). Myeloperoxidase (MPO), a key driver of oxidative inflammation released mainly by activated microglia in the neurodegenerative brain, is a potential therapeutic target to inhibit the neuroinflammatory cascade and oxidative damage in AD, but the underlying mechanisms remain unexplored, and achieving targeted brain delivery of an MPO inhibitor and minimizing systemic effects remain significant challenges. We addressed these limitations by first establishing that genetic deletion of MPO in the 5XFAD mouse model improved memory performance and reduced amyloid deposition, validating MPO as a therapeutic target. We then developed a liposome-encapsulated reactive oxygen species (ROS)-activatable MPO inhibitor (LERAMI). LERAMI uniquely combines targeted delivery with on-demand drug release, utilizing a ROS-sensitive linker to selectively release MPO inhibitors in ROS-rich regions within the AD microenvironment, minimizing off-target effects and systemic toxicity. In the 5XFAD mouse model. By reducing MPO expression and activity, LERAMI significantly improved cognitive performance, accompanied by decreased microglial activation, attenuated oxidative DNA damage, improved synaptic and neuronal density, and reduced amyloid burden. RNA sequencing revealed a robust hippocampal transcriptomic reprogramming, with upregulation of pathways critical for synaptic plasticity, calcium signaling, axon guidance, and neuroprotection, along with downregulation of inflammatory and immune response pathways. These findings demonstrate that targeted ROS-activatable MPO inhibition with LERAMI represents a promising therapeutic strategy for AD and potentially other neuroinflammatory diseases, offering a unique approach to mitigate neuroinflammation, preserve synaptic integrity, and restore cognitive function.

articles.title: Inflammation-Targeted Multifunctional Nanoparticles Remodel the Spinal Cord Injury Microenvironment to Promote Neurovascular Repair.
articles.abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) is characterized by interconnected inflammation, oxidative stress, vascular dysfunction, and impaired neural regeneration, while insufficient lesion-directed delivery further limits the efficacy of systemic therapy. Here, we developed macrophage membrane-camoufl11aged Sr-PDA/Fasudil/MnO2 nanoparticles (MM-NPs) that were designed to integrate inflammation-targeted delivery with complementary immunomodulatory, redox-regulating, and repair-supporting functions. Macrophage membrane camouflage reduced nonspecific phagocytic uptake, enhanced recognition of inflammatory endothelium, improved delivery in an in vitro endothelial barrier model, and increased lesion accumulation in vivo. The formulation provided sustained fasudil release and was designed to combine Rho-associated protein kinase (ROCK) inhibition with redox regulation and bioactive support. MM-NPs consequently attenuated microglial inflammatory activation and excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, improved endothelial migration and angiogenic responses, and alleviated inflammation-induced impairment of neural stem cell differentiation. In a rat SCI model, MM-NPs reduced lesion cavitation and fibrosis, improved the inflammatory microenvironment, enhanced vascular, axonal, and myelin-associated repair, and promoted neurological recovery. Transcriptomic profiling and quantitative spinal cord immunoblotting supported treatment-associated changes in ROCK-associated and NF-κB-related inflammatory signaling. Collectively, MM-NPs couple inflammation-targeted delivery with coordinated immune, redox, vascular, and neural regulation, providing a microenvironment-centered strategy for neurovascular repair after SCI.

articles.title: Hypoxia-activated microglia promote pathological angiogenesis via an FN/ITGB3/FAK/Akt pathway.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To investigate whether hypoxia-activated microglia drive pathological neovascularization through extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling and endothelial integrin signaling, a mechanism that may function in parallel with vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) signaling.
METHODS: The oxygen-induced retinopathy (OIR) mouse model was used. Retinal phenotypes were assessed by flat mounts, histology, and vascular leakage assays. Key pathways were screened by transcriptomics and validated via Western blot, immunofluorescence, and quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR). In vitro, brain microvascular endothelial cells were treated with conditioned medium from hypoxic microglia (Hyp-CM), with cell migration and tube formation assessed. Interventions employed the integrin β3 (ITGB3) inhibitor cilengitide, the focal adhesion kinase (FAK) inhibitor PF-573228 and a neutralizing anti-VEGF antibody. In vivo, cilengitide was administered by intravitreal injection to evaluate its therapeutic effect on neovascularization.
RESULTS: OIR retinas showed significant avascularity, pathological neovascularization, and barrier disruption. Transcriptomics revealed activation of ECM-receptor interaction and focal adhesion pathways, with upregulation of Fn1 and Itgb3. Increased protein levels of fibronectin (FN) and ITGB3, alongside elevated phosphorylation of FAK and protein kinase B (Akt), were confirmed in vivo. Activated microglia co-localized with upregulated FN and ITGB3. Conditioned medium from Hyp-CM activated the ITGB3-FAK-Akt pathway in endothelial cells and promoted their migration and tube formation. These effects were nearly abolished by cilengitide or PF-573228. VEGF neutralization partially reduced Hyp-CM-induced migration and tube formation. Intravitreal injection of cilengitide significantly reduced retinal neovascularization in OIR mice.
CONCLUSION: Hypoxia-activated microglia promote pathological angiogenesis, and the FN/ITGB3/FAK/Akt axis is identified as a key mediator of this process, revealing a novel mechanism that operates in parallel with VEGF signaling. Targeting this "hypoxia-microglia-ECM-integrin" axis represents a promising therapeutic strategy to overcome anti-VEGF resistance in ischemic retinopathy.

articles.title: Long non-coding RNA H19 knockout activates the SAHH/DNMT3b pathway and represses NLRP3 inflammasome expression in a diabetic rat model.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To explore the regulatory effect of long non-coding RNA H19 on the Nod-like receptor protein 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome and its functional role in the progression of diabetic retinopathy (DR).
METHODS: Wild-type and H19 knockout rats were subjected to a high-fat and high-sugar diet combined with streptozotocin injection to establish an in vivo diabetes mellitus (DM) model. In vitro, rat primary retinal microvascular endothelial (CP-R114) cells were cultured under high-glucose conditions to mimic the diabetic microenvironment. The MTS assay was performed to evaluate cell viability. Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) was used to detect the levels of indicators related to glucose metabolism, lipid metabolism, oxidative stress, and inflammation in rat retinal tissues and CP-R114 cells. Hematoxylin and eosin (HE) staining was applied to observe the pathological morphological changes in retinal tissues. qRT-PCR was conducted to quantify the mRNA expression of H19, S-adenosylhomocysteine hydrolase (SAHH), and S-adenosylmethionine-dependent methyltransferase 3 beta (DNMT3b) in rat retinas. Western blotting and immunofluorescence staining were further utilized to detect the protein expression of SAHH, DNMT3b, NLRP3, Caspase-1, and interleukin (IL)-1β in retinal tissues.
RESULTS: In DM model rats, H19 knockout significantly improved glucose and lipid metabolic disorders and alleviated oxidative stress. Notably, H19 deficiency effectively ameliorated retinal tissue injury. The expression levels of intercellular cell adhesion molecule-1 (ICAM-1), vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), and pro-inflammatory factors were markedly downregulated in H19-silenced DM rats. Mechanistically, H19 knockout upregulated the expression of SAHH and DNMT3b, while inhibiting the expression of NLRP3 inflammasome-associated proteins in DM rats. Consistent with the in vivo findings, H19 silencing suppressed NLRP3 inflammasome activation and elevated SAHH and DNMT3b expression in high-glucose-stimulated CP-R114 cells.
CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates that H19 knockout alleviates DR progression in diabetic rats by activating the SAHH/DNMT3b signaling pathway and inhibiting NLRP3 inflammasome activation. Therefore, targeting H19 represents a promising novel therapeutic strategy for the clinical treatment of DR.

articles.title: Disrupting the interaction between T lymphocytes and microglia: Mechanism of Huanglian Jiedu Decoction in the treatment of ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract: Our previous studies have shown that Huanglian Jiedu Decoction effectively suppresses central immune-inflammatory responses, modulates peripheral inflammatory mediators, reduces the infiltration of peripheral T lymphocytes into the central nervous system, and promotes the conversion of infiltrated T lymphocytes in the brain into Treg cells. However, whether Huanglian Jiedu Decoction can influence M2 microglial polarization by regulating T-lymphocyte phenotypic transformation and thereby modulate neuroinflammation after ischemic stroke remains unclear. This study focused on Treg-mediated microglial polarization to investigate the potential of Huanglian Jiedu Decoction to modulate interactions between T lymphocytes and microglia in the treatment of ischemic stroke. We established a rat model of middle cerebral artery occlusion, an inflammatory model of Jurkat T cells stimulated with phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate and ionomycin, and a Transwell co-culture model of T lymphocytes and HMC3 microglia. The results showed that Huanglian Jiedu Decoction effectively alleviated cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury in a rat model of middle cerebral artery, inhibited central inflammatory responses, and promoted the polarization of microglia toward the M2 phenotype. Huanglian Jiedu Decoction also promoted the conversion of CD4+ T cells in brain tissue into regulatory T cells and regulated regulatory T cells through the interleukin-10/Janus kinase 1/signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 pathway, thereby promoting the activation of M2 microglia. These findings suggest that Huanglian Jiedu Decoction, which has heat-clearing and detoxifying properties, can regulate immune homeostasis, inhibit secondary neuroinflammation associated with ischemic stroke, and exert neuroprotective effects. Huanglian Jiedu Decoction may therefore treat ischemic stroke by modulating the interaction between T lymphocytes and microglia, providing a traditional Chinese medicine-based strategy for the treatment of ischemic stroke.

articles.title: Neuroprotective effects of ropinirole against nicotine- and ethanol-induced cognitive impairment, oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and neurodegenerative alterations in rats.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adolescence is a critical period of brain development during which exposure to addictive substances may adversely affect cognitive function and neuronal plasticity. Combined nicotine and ethanol exposure may contribute to persistent cognitive impairment through disturbances in oxidative balance, inflammatory signaling, and hippocampal function. However, the potential effects of pharmacological interventions targeting these alterations after exposure remain insufficiently characterized. Given the previously reported neuroprotective properties of ropinirole, this study investigated whether post-exposure treatment with this dopamine D2/D3 receptor agonist could attenuate cognitive deficits and associated hippocampal biochemical alterations in rats subjected to adolescent nicotine-ethanol co-exposure.
METHODS: Male Wistar rats were exposed to nicotine (2 mg/kg/day, intraperitoneally) and ethanol (20% v/v in drinking water) during adolescence (postnatal days 21-48). Following the exposure period, animals received oral ropinirole at doses of 5, 10, or 20 mg/kg/day for three weeks. Spatial learning and memory and recognition memory were assessed using the Morris water maze and novel object recognition tests, respectively. Hippocampal biochemical assessments included malondialdehyde (MDA), nitrite, total thiol content, superoxide dismutase (SOD), catalase, tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), interleukin-10 (IL-10), brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), acetylcholinesterase (AChE), and amyloid-β (Aβ).
RESULTS: Nicotine-ethanol co-exposure significantly impaired spatial learning, memory retention, and recognition memory, accompanied by increased hippocampal MDA, nitrite, TNF-α, AChE activity, and Aβ levels, together with reduced antioxidant capacity, IL-10, and BDNF expression. Post-exposure ropinirole treatment improved performance in the behavioral tests and attenuated several of the associated biochemical alterations. The 20 mg/kg dose generally showed the most pronounced effects among the doses tested; however, a formal dose-response relationship was not established.
CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that ropinirole exerts neuroprotective effects against adolescent nicotine-ethanol-induced cognitive impairment through the modulation of oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, cholinergic dysfunction, neurotrophic signaling, and amyloid-related pathways. These results provide preliminary evidence supporting dopaminergic modulation as a potential strategy for mitigating substance-associated cognitive dysfunction, although further mechanistic and translational studies are necessary.

articles.title: Integrated Multi-Omics and Machine Learning for Prioritizing Candidate Plasma Proteins in Alzheimer's Disease and Predicting Multi-Target Interactions of Traditional Chinese Medicine.
articles.abstract: This study integrated multi-omics data and machine learning to prioritize candidate plasma proteins and to predict the multi-target interactions of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) in Alzheimer's disease (AD). Mendelian randomization across three cohorts (Icelandic, UK Biobank, and Fenland) identified 66 AD-associated plasma proteins, including TREM2, ACE, GRN, and CR1, with TREM2 showing a robust protective effect (OR = 0.78, 95% CI: 0.75-0.81). Single-cell RNA sequencing showed neuron-specific downregulation of NSF and TMEM106B in AD, implicating synaptic dysfunction and impaired axonal transport. A machine-learning classifier (K-nearest neighbors, KNN) incorporating TREM2, TMEM106B, C1S, PLOD2, and NSF, trained on brain-tissue expression data, demonstrated moderate predictive performance (AUC = 0.76, 95% CI: 0.63-0.90) and is presented as a candidate brain-tissue-derived classifier rather than a validated non-invasive plasma diagnostic panel. Immune infiltration analysis revealed altered M2 macrophage and plasma cell dynamics, with NSF negatively correlated with γδ T-cell infiltration (p < 0.001). Network pharmacology prioritized five candidate TCM herbs (e.g., Scutellaria baicalensis [Huang Qin] and Alpinia oxyphylla [Yi Zhi]) and bioactive compounds (stigmasterol and quercetin) targeting AD-related proteins. Molecular docking predicted strong binding between stigmasterol and PLOD2 (binding energy: -11.2kcal/mol), suggesting a potential role in modulating extracellular matrix remodeling. These compounds were enriched in the PI3K-Akt and NF-κB pathways, consistent with the anti-inflammatory effects observed in TCM formulations such as GHYSJ. These findings link candidate biomarker discovery with the predicted multi-target interactions of TCM, providing hypotheses for future non-invasive diagnosis and precision therapy in AD.

articles.title: Precision immunopharmacology in xenotransplantation: integrating genome-engineered donors, organoid testbeds, and AI-guided translation.
articles.abstract: Xenotransplantation is moving from isolated proof-of-concept procedures toward an engineered biotechnology platform for organ replacement. This review examines how genome-designed donor pigs, recipient-directed immunopharmacology, human-relevant in vitro testbeds, and data-driven decision systems can be integrated to address the remaining barriers to clinical translation. CRISPR-Cas-based engineering enables deletion of dominant carbohydrate xenoantigens, insertion of human complement- and coagulation-regulatory genes, modulation of innate and adaptive immune checkpoints, control of donor-organ growth, and inactivation of porcine endogenous retrovirus sequences. However, donor engineering does not eliminate residual T-cell, B-cell, antibody, complement, natural killer (NK) cell, macrophage, and inflammatory responses. Contemporary immunopharmacological strategies therefore increasingly combine costimulation blockade with complement inhibition, lymphocyte-directed therapy, and selected cytokine- or innate-immune interventions, with future regimens requiring closer integration of pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic monitoring with donor genotype and organ-specific risk. Organoids and microfluidic vascular systems may provide an intermediate testing layer by quantifying antibody binding, complement activation, endothelial injury, coagulation, leukocyte transmigration, cytokine responses, and tissue-specific function under controlled conditions before escalation to large-animal studies. Artificial intelligence may further support xenoantigen discovery, genome-editing design, donor-recipient matching, multimodal rejection surveillance, and ultimately clinician-supervised immunopharmacological decision support. We propose that these components should be connected through a traceable design-build-test-learn workflow linking computational prediction, donor construction, standardized functional testing, non-human-primate validation, and early human data. Durable translation will depend not on any single technological advance, but on reproducible donor manufacturing, precision immune control, validated human-relevant test systems, standardized longitudinal data, pathogen surveillance, organ-specific management, and transparent regulatory governance.

articles.title: Bacteria-responsive programmed antibacterial liposome to modulate the inflammatory microenvironment for intracranial methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus infections.
articles.abstract: For intracranial methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) infections, conventional antibiotics exhibit poor blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability and limited anti-inflammatory activity. To address these challenges, we developed a precisely targeted liposomal system, QAI-lipo, which combines passive BBB accumulation, potent antibiotic-free antibacterial activity, favorable biosafety, and effective modulation of inflammation. Benefiting from lipophilic properties resembling those of cell membranes, QAI-lipo can efficiently cross the BBB. Upon reaching intracranial infection foci, the liposomes are triggered to rupture and release encapsulated payloads by α-toxin secreted by MRSA. Meanwhile, QAI-lipo achieves robust antibacterial effects via dual mechanisms: direct disruption of bacterial membranes and photodynamic action. Animal experiments further verify that QAI-lipo exerts anti-inflammatory activity by inhibiting the MyD88/TRAF-6 signaling pathway, which downregulates the expression of downstream proinflammatory cytokines and upregulates that of anti-inflammatory factors. Moreover, QAI-lipo attenuates the activation of inflammatory cells (including microglia and astrocytes) and suppresses proinflammatory microglial polarization, ultimately improving the survival outcomes of infected animals. This platform offers a general strategy for central nervous system drug delivery and holds promise for broader therapeutic applications, such as the treatment of bacteremia and sepsis.

articles.title: Targeting Energy Metabolism and Tryptophan Pathways in Alzheimer's Disease for Developing Therapeutic Strategies.
articles.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is the primary cause of dementia worldwide and carries a high socioeconomic burden. However, despite the fact that such pathological features as amyloid-beta plaques and neurofibrillary tangles are considered hallmark traits of AD, therapeutic approaches targeting these pathological features have shown limited clinical efficacy to date. Recent scientific discoveries have drawn attention to the importance of metabolic processes preceding neurodegeneration. Reduced glucose utilization and impaired oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) are associated with bioenergetic deficits that may increase neuronal vulnerability to damage. In addition, neuroinflammation is associated with altered tryptophan metabolism through the kynurenine pathway and may favor the production of potentially neurotoxic metabolites. Despite these separate aspects of AD, the interaction between impaired bioenergetics and altered tryptophan metabolism in the brain has not been sufficiently studied. This gap complicates the development of multi-targeted treatment strategies. The purpose of this narrative review is to examine how gut dysbiosis, immune activation, mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) impairment, redox imbalance, and tryptophan-kynurenine pathway dysregulation interact and may contribute to AD development and progression, including associated neuropsychiatric symptoms. We examine whether NAD⁺ depletion and rerouting of tryptophan metabolism may act as key nodes linking mitochondrial respiratory failure with the generation of neurotoxic kynurenine metabolites, excitotoxic glutamatergic signaling, loss of neurotrophic support, and synaptic dysfunction, and to analyze existing and emerging therapeutic strategies that target these interconnected pathways. In addition, this review highlights potentially promising interventions, such as NAD⁺ precursor supplementation, central nervous system insulin delivery, and modification of gut microbiome. Here we propose that the energy-tryptophan metabolic axis is a promising but underexplored area of AD research. Targeting these convergent bioenergetic and metabolomic pathways may support precision intervention strategies that could extend beyond conventional amyloid-centric paradigms to address broader neurodegenerative and neuropsychiatric syndromes.

articles.title: Metabolic reprogramming of macrophage-specific transketolase orchestrates angiogenesis in diabetic wounds.
articles.abstract: Diabetic wound healing is profoundly impaired by macrophage metabolic dysfunction, which compromises angiogenesis. Here, we show a macrophage transketolase (TKT) as a crucial metabolic checkpoint governing vascular regeneration in diabetes. We demonstrate that loss of TKT in macrophages accelerates amino acid and fatty acid catabolism, elevates reactive oxygen species, and disrupts endothelial cell proliferation and differentiation. Mechanistically, hyperglycemia activates the AGEs-RAGE signaling cascade through suppressing TKT expression, establishing a pathological TKT-AGEs-RAGE axis that reprograms macrophage metabolism toward dysfunction. Then, we engineer a nanozyme-integrated hydrogel patch that selectively increases TKT level in macrophages, which rebalances macrophage metabolism, reduces oxidative stress, and rescues angiogenic capacity. In a diabetic pig model, localized delivery of the nano-system markedly accelerates wound closure and vascular repair. These findings not only elucidate a macrophage-specific TKT metabolic reprogramming mechanism for enhancing angiogenesis, but also offer a potential therapeutic strategy for the clinical management of diabetic wounds.
